title: Branching proof structure: a synthetic renderer fixture
scope: Synthetic structure for regression testing: two main results, separate coverage assumptions, one alternative regime, and an explicitly reused proof argument. This fixture does not assert a proved mathematical theory.

source.title: Synthetic declarations supplied with the test fixture

statement.text: The variables have finite second moments.
$\mathcal F$ is the collection indexing the estimators.
The empirical average has the stated population expectation.
The variance of the empirical average is bounded by the claimed finite-sample expression.
The centered average obeys the stated pointwise probability bound.
The pointwise probability bound tends to zero.
A finite approximation of $\mathcal F$ controls the remaining supremum.
The estimator obeys the stated uniform convergence rate over $\mathcal F$.

For every deterministic sequence of centers and every permitted perturbation, the absolute error is bounded by the sum of the approximation term and the perturbation term. The supremum is over the complete index class, and the bound uses the same realization of the observations for every index. The centers are deterministic, the variance normalization is strictly positive, the envelope has the stipulated integrable moment, and the approximation remainder converges to zero uniformly. The constants may depend on the moment bound and on the fixed index class, but do not depend on $n$, the evaluation index, or the chosen deterministic centers. In the conditional version, the observations are independent of the training data given the designated training sigma-field; each measurability and conditional moment requirement is retained. Only the absolute-error argument in the proof is reused by the following transfer result. The separate ratio conclusion is not assumed in that application. All listed restrictions belong to this intentionally long synthetic statement and must remain accessible in the full details even when the pointer preview is abbreviated.
The absolute-error bound transfers to the perturbed estimator without using the ratio conclusion.
The pilot sample is independent of the evaluation sample.
The stability claim holds in the stated deterministic regime or the separately qualified pilot-trained regime.
The approximation and quantile conditions required for band coverage hold.
The distributional approximation has the error required by the quantile argument.
Under the separate coverage conditions, the simultaneous band attains its stated limiting coverage.
